name: Copernicus
narrative: A young crater with terraced walls and tall central peaks. Those peaks are deep material pushed up by the impact, so Copernicus is a natural drill core into the Moon's crust.
note: The USGS Gazetteer lists 93.00 km and 96.07 km under different control networks; 93 km is used here. Depth and age are not listed by the Gazetteer, so they are shown as not verified.

name: South Pole-Aitken Basin
narrative: The Moon's largest and deepest basin, spanning nearly a quarter of the surface. The impact that made it was so tremendous that scientists expect it to have pierced through the crust and into the mantle, which is why it is a prime target for sample return.
note: NASA gives the diameter as more than 2,500 km and the average depth as about 10 km.

name: Tycho
narrative: One of the Moon's brightest craters, at the centre of the most extensive ray system on the near side. Its sharp rim and bright ejecta mark it as young, and its rays stretch for hundreds of kilometres across the surface.
note: Gazetteer-linked sources cite 85–86 km for the diameter; 85 km is used here. Depth and age are not listed by the Gazetteer, so they are shown as not verified.
